# myArc

> A pre-release open-source browser project inspired by Arc, built on Chromium with a Rust-owned workspace core.

A complete myArc browser remains unimplemented, and the Arc importer brings over only Spaces and pinned tabs. Native integration is experimental. Arc reference screenshots illustrate the target appearance. Local ownership and optional AI are product requirements, not evidence of a finished release.

## Project

- [Overview](https://myarc.dev/index.md): Markdown equivalent of the homepage.
- [Progress journal](https://myarc.dev/blog/index.md): Published development updates.
- [Download](https://myarc.dev/download/index.md): Pre-alpha nightly status, requirements and known limitations.
- [Repository](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc): Public source and plans.

## Posts

- [Letting agents use myArc](https://myarc.dev/blog/agents-use-myarc/index.md): The agents that build myArc can now use it, in a Space of their own and only after you say yes. Getting there turned up a bug in Chromium and a sidebar full of gray globes.
- [One window, two profiles](https://myarc.dev/blog/one-window-two-profiles/index.md): myArc now has real Profiles, so Work and Personal keep their own cookies and logins. Getting them to live in one window, the way Arc did, took more than I expected.
- [Taking a few patches from ungoogled-chromium](https://myarc.dev/blog/ungoogled-chromium/index.md): myArc now borrows four build flags and five patches from ungoogled-chromium. I left out the patches that would cost myArc more than they give, like the ones that break the Chrome Web Store.
- [Chasing Arc's details](https://myarc.dev/blog/closer-to-arc/index.md): Side-by-side recordings showed what myArc's sidebar was missing, and a quit bug was emptying every Space. Next up is an alpha checklist.
- [Why myArc is now GPL-3.0](https://myarc.dev/blog/gpl/index.md): myArc moved from the MIT license to GPL-3.0 so it stays open for good. I don't plan to make money from it, and any modified version has to publish its code.
- [Building myArc in public](https://myarc.dev/blog/building-in-public/index.md): Why I'm building myArc after Arc's sunset announcement, with account-free browsing, no behavioral tracking and an Artcraft-inspired workflow.
